e8b_medium_ledger.scope: every MEDIUM and LOW finding from the three review lenses of the previous round, plus findings raised in this session, each classified and dispositioned. No finding is silently dismissed.

classification_rules.execution-critical: must be fixed before any core training
classification_rules.scientific-validity: must be fixed, or proven not to affect the frozen primary protocol
classification_rules.provenance/reproducibility: must be fixed where it affects reconstruction
classification_rules.reporting/documentation: may remain only if scheduled for dissertation cleanup and cannot mislead execution

entries.issue: Frozen LM training-path numerics change bf16->fp32 under autocast; A1_precision said training 'unchanged' and nothing pinned the LM training dtype
entries.evidence: build_core_recipe now carries training_precision AND frozen_lm_instance_dtype explicitly, both inside recipe_sha256. Under bf16 autocast every per-op operand is the exactly-representable pinned bf16 value, so the training math equals the pinned-bf16 construction; this is stated in the recipe rather than assumed.

entries.issue: build_core_recipe still emitted max_epochs 100 and patience 10 for B2/B3, contradicting the fixed-22 decision, and the budget sat outside the hash
entries.evidence: B2/B3 recipes now carry max_epochs 22, early_stopping False, patience 'disabled', canonical_checkpoint_rule epoch_22 and primary_checkpoint_selection fixed_endpoint, all INSIDE recipe_sha256. Protocol family bumped to e8b-fp32-fixed22-core-2026-08-07 so any earlier recipe/checkpoint fails resume.

entries.issue: assert_lm_buffer_parity had no runnable call site; the OI5 pair check never executed
entries.evidence: Called in preflight on the two live inventories AND in _train_core_locked for every B2/B3 cell, comparing this arm against its counterpart, after construction and before the first optimizer step.

entries.issue: Fixing the epoch count equalises draws but not max-over-epochs selection bias (~0.008-0.010/cell), which does not cancel in B3-B2; no selection-free estimator planned
entries.evidence: Superseded by the user's fixed-endpoint decision: the primary checkpoint is epoch 22, not the max over epochs, so there is no max-over-epochs selection bias in the primary contrast at all. Best-of-22 survives only as a labelled secondary diagnostic that cannot determine the primary comparison, the freeze or the clean-test checkpoint. Per-row canonical predictions are dumped for paired tests.

entries.issue: B1 keeps patience-10/max-100 while B2/B3 are fixed, so B1-involving contrasts retain the run-length confound
entries.evidence: The user's decision F is explicit that B1 retains its frozen section 7.3 recipe and must not be forced onto the 22-epoch rule. B1 is an interface-width control, not part of the primary B3-B2 contrast, which is unaffected. The asymmetry is recorded in the recipe (B1 canonical_checkpoint_rule = best dev accuracy, section 7.3 inherited) and in CLAUDE.md.
entries.closed_by: training.py build_core_recipe B1 branch; CLAUDE.md gate item 5

entries.issue: lm.config.dtype and generation_config differed between the paired arms and were covered by no hash or pair check
entries.evidence: load_frozen_causal_lm now normalises config.dtype for both arms and loads generation_config from the pinned snapshot for both, so no frozen state other than the parameter values differs across the pair. Both are recorded in provenance.

entries.issue: Resource projection and abandonment evidence had no committed generator; npz untracked; B1 hours not reproducible
entries.evidence: core_resource_projection.py and determinism_call_scan.py are committed generators that regenerate their records; the npz is force-added; B1 hours now derive from the MEASURED 86.36 s/epoch 250k rate rather than a step-scaled guess.

entries.issue: Supersession map incomplete: u4_decision.json still PROMOTE, protocol_clarification still authorised grid 2-8, preregistration U4_OPEN, g14_v2_preregistration contradicted the amendment
entries.evidence: superseded_evidence_20260807.json now carries 14 records including all four, each with why-wrong and replacement. Source files preserved verbatim; live constants carry the withdrawal.

entries.issue: dev_r1_predictions (the BF16 selection function) survived and was still wired into the only training loop and both G14 invocations
entries.evidence: dev_r1_predictions is DELETED. The only evaluation entry points are canonical_dev_predictions (LM arms) and b1_canonical_predictions (B1), both fp32 with fail-closed dtype gates. The search trainer that called it is deleted too.

entries.issue: The timing anchoring every projection was measured without GPU-exclusivity and without a run lock
entries.evidence: determinism_probe now asserts GPU exclusivity before timing anything and asserts its own non-scientific authorisation constant. Probe runs 3/4 (the timing source) were measured on an idle exclusive GPU.

entries.issue: G14-FP32 validated at chunk size 64, not the canonical 128
entries.evidence: The gate now chunks at 128, the canonical evaluation batch size named in the frozen specification.

entries.issue: The abandoned search was refused only at the CLI; train_search_point had no authorisation guard, and the probe bypassed authorisation
entries.evidence: train_search_point, train_pilot and _train_locked are DELETED, so no search execution path exists at any entry. The probe asserts NONSCIENTIFIC_PROBE_AUTHORIZED. Every scientific entry refuses on TRAINING_AUTHORIZED.

entries.issue: Storage gate declared passed against free space, reversing the E8A record that declared the allocation UNRESOLVED
entries.evidence: The storage gate now records status UNRESOLVED with the free-space check reported separately as context, matching the E8A precedent.

entries.issue: remaining_core_hours gated against the 180 h ceiling but covered only E8B
entries.evidence: Renamed e8b_remaining_vs_180h_core with an explicit scope_note stating it covers E8B cells and E8B evaluation only, and naming the remaining E8A component.

entries.issue: The 22-epoch budget was selected from observed search results, contradicting A3's claim that no selection was performed on any observed result
entries.evidence: The recipe now separates the two: fixed_hyperparameters_justification (lr/warmup/dropout retained PRE-RESULT) and epoch_budget_justification (a DATED POST-DIAGNOSTIC amendment fixed after seeing best epochs 20/11/6). The distinction is inside the hashed recipe.

entries.issue: 'Strict determinism costs 45 per cent' was confounded with the FP32 promotion and the SDPA backend change
entries.evidence: Relabelled amended_design_cost_note: the 78.0 vs 53.88 s/epoch difference is the TOTAL cost of the amended design relative to the superseded one, bundling three simultaneous changes, and is not attributed to any single one.

entries.issue: The identity headroom carried no re-run budget
entries.evidence: retry_allowance now records NONE explicitly: the plan tolerates zero B3 retries and any retry or extra B3-loading evaluation triggers a stop-and-ask before execution.

entries.issue: assert_canonical_scores was vacuous; the frozen-LM dtype check sampled a single parameter
entries.evidence: assert_canonical_scores now also enforces finiteness (a NaN would otherwise pass every threshold and sail through argmax). canonical_prefix checks the FULL dtype set of both the trainable model and the frozen LM, not one sampled parameter.

entries.issue: G14 halt details omitted questionId/imageId; the record omitted the minimum margin
entries.evidence: g14_fp32_gate takes dev_frame and records questionId and imageId in every halt detail; dev_margin_quantiles now includes min.

entries.issue: canonical_prefix's autocast guard did not see CPU autocast
entries.evidence: torch.is_autocast_enabled('cpu') added to the guard.

entries.issue: g14_fp32_gate checked only the length of the supplied margins
entries.evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-07: G14-FP32 now REQUIRES an evaluation binding at the post-selection stage and re-verifies it against the live model, recomputing the model-state digest and the margin digest and halting on any mismatch. The binding carries the model-state digest, recipe SHA, protocol family, evaluation precision, prediction and margin digests, row count and scorer source digest, so a record whose margins cannot be proven to belong to the evaluated state fails closed.
entries.closed_by: training.py evaluation_binding + g14_fp32_gate binding re-verification; known-negative tests

entries.issue: determinism_probe.compare() truncated silently on unequal epoch counts and did not compare the determinism/precision blocks
entries.evidence: compare() now hard-exits on any epoch-count mismatch and compares the determinism and fp32_precision blocks in run_level_checks.

entries.issue: save_resume_checkpoint stamped the module protocol_family unconditionally
entries.evidence: protocol_family is now a required keyword argument taken from the recipe, so a run can only stamp its own family.

entries.issue: Non-buffer frozen state outside the OI5 inventory differed between arms
entries.evidence: Same fix as A-M6: config.dtype normalised and generation_config pinned for both arms.

entries.issue: CLAUDE.md materially stale ('Phase 1 has not begun')
entries.evidence: Replaced with a dated, binding seven-point E8B gate covering the abandoned search, the fixed recipe, withdrawn U4, FP32 canonical evaluation, the epoch-22 endpoint rule, the determinism discipline and the refusal of scientific execution.

entries.issue: The determinism probe's GPU time was not charged anywhere
entries.evidence: spent_compute() itemises probes 1-4 from their own recorded walls and charges them to the pretrained identity.

entries.issue: B1's per-cell hours used a step-scaled 250k rate rather than the measured one; B1 final evaluation was charged at the LM R1 pass rate
entries.evidence: B1 now uses the MEASURED 86.36 s/epoch 250k rate from section 13.2; the B1 final-evaluation line is explicitly labelled an upper bound and never touches an identity ceiling because B1 loads no LM.

entries.issue: The selection-sensitivity study (22 checkpoints x R2/R3 = 44 passes) was still costed although the fixed-endpoint rule voids its object
entries.evidence: Recorded VOID under the fixed-22 epoch-22-canonical rule and removed from the projection; reinstating any analogue requires a fresh user decision and a fresh projection.

entries.issue: CORE_FIXED_JUSTIFICATION stated only that the recipe was the pre-result default and did not disclose that the same configuration also showed the highest bf16 development maximum of the three grid points that completed. A reader of the code alone could not see the coincidence and judge it.
entries.evidence: training.CORE_FIXED_JUSTIFICATION now carries the disclosure explicitly, framed exactly as CLAUDE.md gate item 2 requires: exploratory, NON-CANONICAL, SUPERSEDED, invalidated for ranking because the pools differ in length, and offered as support for nothing. The stated reason for the freeze remains SOLELY that it was the pre-result preregistered default, and the freeze is outcome-independent by construction.
entries.closed_by: the user's item-7 instruction of 2026-08-07, which governs over the reviewer's plainer wording

entries.issue: The G8 overfit gate trains to a convergence threshold and so consumes a different number of RNG draws in B2 than in B3. The paired arms therefore entered the training loop on divergent global RNG states, so their dropout masks and shuffle orders differed for a reason unrelated to the pretrained-versus-random contrast that B3 minus B2 exists to isolate. The loader generator was re-seeded after the gate; the global RNG was not.
entries.evidence: training.py re-seeds with e8b_run.reseed_strict(recipe['seed']) after the G8/G14 gates and before the resume block, so both arms enter training on a common RNG state; the placement before the resume block preserves resume fidelity, since a resume legitimately overwrites RNG from the saved state. Ordering is asserted in tests (gate < reseed < loop, and reseed < resume).

entries.issue: history, train_times and eval_times were not resume fields. The fixed-endpoint rule reads history[-1] to identify the epoch-22 canonical checkpoint, so a cell resumed at or near the final epoch would die on an IndexError inside a loop that would then retry and die again, or would select a canonical epoch from a truncated record.
entries.evidence: run.RESUME_FIELDS now carries history, train_times and eval_times; save_resume_checkpoint requires them and restore_resume_state returns them; training.py restores them on resume. The empty-history path halts through gate_halt with the reason stated instead of raising IndexError. Superseded pre-amendment checkpoints stay READABLE FOR AUDIT via protocol_family=None but cannot be restored, which is asserted as a known negative.

entries.issue: B1Classifier.forward returned AttentionPoolReadout's (logits, attention_weights) pair unchanged, while every B1 consumer -- the loss, the dtype gate, the shape gate and the canonical evaluation -- expects a tensor. All six B1 core cells would have acquired the NFS lock, hashed the token stores and then died with an uncaught AttributeError, with no HALT and no FAILED record.
entries.evidence: B1Classifier.forward now unpacks and returns logits only; forward_with_weights keeps the diagnostic pair. Reproduced before the fix and asserted after it by a REAL forward and backward pass, not a source-text check -- which is why the defect survived: every prior B1 test was a hasattr or substring assertion.

entries.issue: Strict determinism was downgraded for the whole of both overfit gates. utils.set_seed sets warn_only=True and the builders re-seed again, so optimizer.step ran for up to 200 epochs with enforcement downgraded, inside a HALTING gate, while the hashed recipe recorded strict enforcement throughout. Confirmed empirically by reading the live flag.
entries.evidence: both gates now call reseed_strict at entry, re-impose after the internal builder re-seed, and assert at the point of use.

entries.issue: Resume verified the recipe hash and protocol family but never the implementation, though code_head was stored from the beginning. A cell could crash at epoch 14, have a defect fixed, resume, and run epochs 15-22 under different code, producing an epoch-22 canonical checkpoint spliced from two implementations.
entries.evidence: verify_resume_checkpoint now compares code_head AND a new code_digest over the E8B sources, so a dirty -worktree edit that leaves the commit unchanged is caught too.

entries.issue: The 35 GPU-hour per-model-identity ceiling and the storage gate, both re-ratified as hard halts, had no call site in the execution path. Nothing summed GPU hours across cells, so the ceiling could only ever have been checked by hand.
entries.evidence: run.per_identity_gate reads an append-only ledger and is checked before every cell against its projected cost and after it against measured hours, which are charged; run.storage_gate is checked before every cell; both halt through gate_halt. The gate reproduces the published 32.960 h and fires between a 16 and 17 per cent overrun on the 250k rate.

entries.issue: G14_ROW_S 5.301 and R2_ROW_S 0.0291 were emitted under keys naming them MEASURED, but neither is traceable to any E8B artefact: the recorded G14 per-row costs are 5.149/5.137/5.135 and no E8B R2 readout has ever run.
entries.evidence: both are relabelled as ASSUMPTIONS with their real basis stated (pooled 5.139 plus a 3 per cent margin; R2 carried over from the E7b S8 per-row cost), and their sensitivity is quantified.

entries.issue: The record claimed to cover the COMPLETE planned pretrained-identity programme while omitting the mandatory section-19 serial efficiency measurement, which loads the pretrained language model and is costed at 0.500-1.000 h.
entries.evidence: the pass is charged at its upper bound; the pretrained identity rises from 31.960 to 32.960 h and the headroom falls from 3.04 to 2.04 h. A correction UPWARD against the ceiling.

entries.issue: The anchor caveat claimed 'both files are tracked and the worktree was clean'. The checkpoint is git-ignored and has never been in git, so its hash is a first-and-only self-attestation, not a corroborated anchor.
entries.evidence: the caveat now quotes its own erroneous sentence and records the verified tracking status of each artefact separately, stating what each anchor is and is not worth. The tests now HASH both files instead of string-matching the digests inside the record.

entries.issue: determinism_probe_run1/run2/comparison record 'warn_only': false and 'STRICT DETERMINISM CONFIRMED' for runs the project has itself established ran under warn_only=True, with no in-file marker; the correction existed only in an external map.
entries.evidence: each file now carries a leading SUPERSEDED block naming the withdrawn claim, the replacement artefacts, the only reliable discriminator (verified_at_use) and the fact that the hours remain charged. Original content is unmodified below it.

entries.issue: The per-identity and storage gates were computed in train_core_cell but read in _train_core_locked, which does not receive them, so identity_gate and storage were unbound globals. Every core cell would have trained to completion, written its canonical checkpoint and per-row dump, then died with an uncaught NameError while assembling the result -- before the ledger charge and before the result was written. No result, no charge, no HALT and no FAILED record, and the re-run would then refuse at the existing npz. INTRODUCED BY THE FIX FOR AUDIT-C-HIGH-1.
entries.evidence: the gate results are passed as parameters; asserted by disassembling _train_core_locked and checking that no gate name is read as LOAD_GLOBAL, and by asserting none of them is a module global.

entries.issue: charge_identity_hours was reachable only after every gate passed, and every gate_halt is a sys.exit, so the hours burned by a halted or crashed cell were never charged. A cell that ran 7.9 hours and tripped the wall would vanish from the ledger and the 35-hour ceiling would green-light the next cell on an identity that had already spent the headroom.
entries.evidence: the charge moved into train_core_cell's finally block, so it runs on every exit path, and the ledger now records ONE ENTRY PER PROCESS rather than a single overwritten total, which is what makes charging on every path safe without double-counting a resume.

entries.issue: e8b_code_digest omitted src/reasoner.py, which defines the trunk architecture -- precisely the dirty-worktree splice the digest exists to catch, and the realistic case, since every 2026-08-07 record has git_dirty true.
entries.evidence: the digest now covers all of src/, config.py and the E8A modules the core path imports, not only the E8B directory.

entries.issue: The resumed-cell wall carried only per-epoch train and eval time, so store hashing, the LM load and promotion, G8 and G14 pre-selection were bought back free on every crash-resume cycle. Ledger corruption raised uncaught exceptions with no halt artefact, and the ledger lived on node-local scratch while the duplicate-run lock deliberately does not.
entries.evidence: the wall now reads every prior process's full wall from the ledger; an unreadable or malformed ledger REFUSES rather than assuming zero hours spent; and the ledger moved to the shared filesystem beside the execution locks.

entries.issue: The 180 GPU-hour core ceiling was still not executable: remaining_core_gate had no call site outside tests, the identical defect that had just been closed for the 35-hour ceiling.
entries.evidence: core_remaining_hours derives the remaining hours from the governing projection minus everything charged to the ledger, and train_core_cell halts on it before any GPU work.

entries.issue: restore_resume_state mutated the model, optimizer, scheduler and all four RNG streams before raising on a legacy checkpoint, leaving a half-restored process; and the overfit gates verified determinism into a variable that was then discarded, so the verified state never reached any record.
entries.evidence: restore validates the full field set before touching anything, and both gates record their verified determinism block in the gate record.

entries.issue: The fix for AUDIT-C-HIGH-2 replaced a mislabel with a FALSE PROVENANCE. It claimed R2 0.0291 s/row was carried over from the E7b S8-stage per-row cost. The E7b figure is S8_projection = 0.0291 MILLISECONDS, a LayerNorm-plus-Linear projection stage: a different operation in units 1000x apart. The matching digits are a coincidence, and R3 was derived from it.
entries.evidence: both rates are declared UNSOURCED, the false claim is quoted and corrected in the generator and in the reconciliation, and NO replacement provenance was invented. The exposure is quantified and listed as an OPEN RISK for the user to accept or close with a measurement.

entries.issue: The 'complete planned programme' claim was still false. Canonical plan section 6 requires every readout evaluation to run once over the 10,004-row RAW denominator and section 6.1 requires every final checkpoint to receive raw-distribution evaluation; the projection budgeted 7,714 in-vocabulary rows and HB3b was neither implemented nor budgeted. Section 7 applies three matched intervention conditions to EVERY trained checkpoint, B1 included, and B1's 18 intervention passes were omitted.
entries.evidence: N_RAW = 10004 is charged for R2, R3 and a raw-distribution R1 pass per cell, and B1 is charged its three intervention conditions. The pretrained identity rises from 32.960 to 33.472 h and the headroom falls to 1.528 h. A correction UPWARD.

entries.issue: The G14 per-row input was presented as conservative, but its measurement covers R1 brute force plus R1 cached only, while the live gate also runs r2_brute_force and r2_cached per row under clause C3. The 3.15 per cent margin does not cover two extra constrained walks over 224 rows and 12 cells, so the input is optimistic.
entries.evidence: the shortfall is stated in the generator and listed as an OPEN, UNQUANTIFIED risk in the reconciliation rather than described as a conservative margin.

entries.issue: A live record still certified the superseded 31.96 h / 3.04 h headroom figure, and four further records the project's own map treats as superseded carried no in-file marker: u4_decision.json still reading PROMOTE, protocol_clarification still authorising grid points 2 to 8, g14_v2_preregistration, and preregistration.json carrying U4_OPEN.
entries.evidence: all five carry in-place additive markers naming what is superseded, what still stands and what replaced it; original content is unmodified below each marker.

entries.issue: The FP32 amendment's withdrawal block said 'the text below states', but both texts it corrects appear ABOVE it, so the correction misdirected the reader. Several quantified sensitivities were also internally inconsistent with their own carried-hours figures, and the container key measured_inputs held four entries that are not measurements.
entries.evidence: the block states ABOVE and carries a placement note; the sensitivities are computed from the same constants they describe rather than hand-written; and the container carries an explicit note that not every entry is a measurement.

entries.issue: A THIRD instance of the unbound-name defect, again introduced by the previous fix: moving the ledger charge into the caller's finally block left the trailing [LEDGER] print and the post-charge halt behind, still referencing a name that now lived in the caller. All 18 cells would have trained to completion, written every artefact, then died with NameError before returning.
entries.evidence: the leftover block was removed and a bytecode binding sweep over every function, method, nested function and comprehension on the executable path now runs as a test. It found this instance; reading the code had missed the same class three times.

entries.issue: preflight() called save_resume_checkpoint without the four arguments that had become required two commits earlier, so --preflight would have died with a TypeError after minutes of GPU work. The same block would then have failed verification and restore for the same reason. No test executed preflight.
entries.evidence: the call site passes protocol_family, history, train_times and eval_times, and a static arity sweep now binds EVERY internal call against its callee's live signature.

entries.issue: The finally-block charge could destroy the failure that brought execution there: read_spend_ledger is fail-closed and raises `from None`, so an unreadable ledger would replace a CUDA OOM with a JSONDecodeError, leave the cell lock held, and write no artefact.
entries.evidence: the lock is released FIRST, and every accounting step is contained: an accounting failure writes a G19_LEDGER halt record and is reported, never raised, so the original failure survives.

entries.issue: The code digest hashed every file in src/, the E8A directory and the E8B directory, most of which cannot affect a trajectory, and code_head equality was ALSO required. Any commit during a run -- including one to a report -- would have invalidated every outstanding resume, and since the ledger charges every process and never refunds, one crash plus one commit on a 250k cell could push the identity past its ceiling.
entries.evidence: the digest covers a FIXED list of eleven trajectory sources, including src/reasoner.py, and refuses if any is absent rather than silently covering less than it claims. The digest is the authority; a differing code_head with byte-identical sources is reported and recorded, not treated as a prohibition.

entries.issue: charge_identity_hours was an unsynchronised read-modify-write to a shared ledger through a FIXED temporary filename, so two concurrent cells could drop each other's charge -- the exact under-count the ceiling exists to prevent.
entries.evidence: the whole read-modify-write runs under an exclusive ledger lock with a per-process staged filename, and refuses rather than writing unsynchronised if the lock is held too long. Verified with 24 concurrent charges: none lost.

entries.issue: Two halting paths raised bare AssertionErrors without the halt artefact the protocol requires, and a resumed cell did not check its wall budget until the first training step, so an already-exhausted cell would re-run the model load, the parity load, G8 and G14 pre-selection before it could halt.
entries.evidence: the core gate writes a halt record before raising, and the wall is checked before the loop on a resumed cell.
